newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem vows defiance against strikers.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem vows defiance against strikers.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem pledged Tuesday that his government's economic policies will not be swayed by the 36-hour general strike starting Thursday.
"We are going to demonstrate here that the one giving the orders is the government that was elected by the people," Menem told a meeting of the Chamber of Private Pension Funds.
Menem dismissed the strike as "a holiday" for unionists, but said that it could cost the country up to $1.7 billion. He added that a previous 24-hour stoppage in August had cost Argentina $1 billion.
However, Menem said: "There is no possibility of having changes imposed which go against the will of the people."

The strike is being led by the CGT union confederation, which is usually close to the governing Peronist Party. But, angry at unemployment of 17.1 percent, it is fighting Menem's drive for fiscal austerity and more flexible labor laws.
CGT heads are due to attend a Peronist Party meeting later Tuesday, but said they will not call off the strike.
